correctness.rationale: Meet-preserving, top-preserving, deflationary idempotents on finite L correspond exactly to bounded sublattices S via f_S(x)=largest s∈S below x. For L=C₂×C_n, meet/join closure permits exactly occupied-column words A^a C^c B^b with empty-column gaps; endpoints force inclusion of 0 and 1. Choosing occupied m columns and c doubles gives coefficient binomial(n−2,m−2)×(m−c+1−2·1[c=0]) at rank m+c, proving the sum and bivariate rational function for all n≥2. Independently enumerated every bounded subset using separate meet/join closure for n=2..6: total 4,12,33,86,216 and matching exact rank histograms; n=2 counts u²+2u³+u⁴. This finite verification is secondary to the bijection and exact word proof. Source Kavvos Definition 4.1 gives equivalence between stable bimodules and modal meet-right-adjoints on nonempty filters.

originality.rationale: Kavvos arXiv:2406.03578 supplies the stable-bimodule modal correspondence, not the two-row fixed-filter rank census. OEIS A341867 exactly has the ungraded row total, which is explicitly excluded from novelty. The entire fixed-filter rank refinement with rational bivariate series and canonical S4 family is the surviving distinct contribution; it may be an unindexed rank-refined bounded-sublattice enumeration.
residual_risks: An unindexed graded rank polynomial for bounded sublattices of a two-row product may cover these coefficients.
Limited to labeled frames W=C₂×C_n and T/4 stable bimodules; does not classify all S4 modalities on higher width or arbitrary frames.

value.rationale: Fixed-filter rank is intrinsic to the modal semantics, rather than an artificial statistic. The result classifies how many filters a stable S4 necessity modality fixes on the natural first branching two-row lattice, gives all possible ranks 2..2n and exact extremal classes; the finite family is parameterized by arbitrary n.
